_meta.source: https://www.lakshadweeptourism.com/ (official site of SPORTS — Society for Promotion of Nature Tourism and Sports, the Lakshadweep Administration's nodal tourism agency, formed 1982)
_meta.scope: Lakshadweep Union Territory — the tourist 'focal' islands and how to visit them
_meta.note: SPORTS site is a small static site (last visible copyright 2007) and is thin on entry-permit detail; permit facts below are taken from the official Lakshadweep Administration / ePermit portal and India.gov.in, not invented. Rules for foreign nationals changed in 2026 — travellers must check epermit.utl.gov.in for the current position.

basicFacts.status: Smallest Union Territory of India; India's only coral-island chain; a single district
basicFacts.composition: 36 islands; 12 atolls, 3 reefs, 5 submerged banks. Total land area ~32 sq km. Lagoons enclosed by the atolls ~4,200 sq km. Territorial waters ~20,000 sq km; EEZ ~400,000 sq km.
basicFacts.location: Arabian Sea, ~220 to 440 km off the Kerala coast, between 8 deg and 12 deg N and 71 deg and 74 deg E. Connected to the mainland only from Kochi (Cochin).
basicFacts.climate: Tropical. Summer 22-33 C, winter 20-32 C. Southwest monsoon June-September brings heavy rain; Oct-May is the pleasant, calmer period.
basicFacts.people: Predominantly Muslim population; Malayalam is the main language, with Mahl (Dhivehi, written in Thaana) spoken on Minicoy.
basicFacts.ecoAward: SPORTS received the Union Ministry of Tourism's 'most eco-friendly organisation' award for 1996-97.

entryPermit.required: YES — mandatory for every visitor who is not a native islander (Indian citizens included). Governed by the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands (Restriction on Entry and Residence) Rules, 1967.
entryPermit.howToApply: Online via the official ePermit portal epermit.utl.gov.in — register, choose the 'Tourist' category, enter travel dates and the islands to be visited, and upload ID proof and a photograph. Apply well ahead (guidance widely cited as at least ~14 days before travel). Sponsorship is no longer required for Tourist-category applications.
entryPermit.historicalRequirement: A police clearance certificate from the applicant's local station was historically required; from 2026 this and local sponsorship were relaxed for many applicants — CHECK the current rule on epermit.utl.gov.in before travelling.
entryPermit.foreignNationals: Need a valid passport and Indian visa. Historically foreigners could visit only a limited set of islands (commonly cited: Agatti, Bangaram, Thinnakara, Kadmat); the SPORTS site notes Kadmat specifically that 'Non Indians are also permitted to visit this island', and the Samudram cruise is open to foreign nationals holding a tourist visa. Access rules for foreigners changed in 2026 — verify the current position on the ePermit portal.

howToReach.air: Only airstrip is on AGATTI. Flights operated from Kochi (Cochin) to Agatti; flight time ~1 hr 30 min. From Agatti, onward to Bangaram/Thinnakara by boat (or helicopter, season permitting) and to Kavaratti/Kadmat by boat during the fair season (~October to May).
howToReach.sea: Passenger ships from Kochi only. Vessels cited by SPORTS: MV Kavaratti, MV Arabian Sea, MV Lakshadweep Sea, MV Lagoons, MV Corals (other government vessels e.g. MV Amindivi, MV Minicoy also serve the sector). Passage ~14-20 hours depending on the island. Classes: A/C First Class (2-berth cabins), A/C Second Class (4-berth cabins), plus bunk/seat classes. A doctor is available on call on board. Ships are not offered for tourist transport during the monsoon (mid-May to September) — local passengers only.
howToReach.interIsland: From Agatti, boats to Kavaratti and Kadmat run in the fair season (Oct-May). You may not leave your island's lagoon without SPORTS permission and a proper escort.

touristSeason.monsoon: Mid-May to September — sea rough, ship tourist services suspended; Kadmat, Minicoy and Kavaratti resorts hard to reach as they have no flight/helicopter link. Agatti/Bangaram flights continue year-round.
touristSeason.quote: The best time to visit Lakshadweep is from October to mid May. From mid May to September it is rainy.

waterSports.islandWide: All islands in the tourist packages offer kayaks, canoes, pedal boats, sail boats, wind surfers, snorkel sets and glass-bottomed boats.

scubaDiving.note: Calm lagoon ideal for beginners; giant sea fans, turtles, soft corals, reef sharks, rays, tropical fish.
Beginner to instructor CMAS courses, season ~1 October to 1 May; visibility 20-50 m; regarded as one of India's finest dive sites.

waterSports.deepSeaFishing: Big-game fishing for barracuda, sailfish, yellowfin tuna, trevally and sharks.

tourPackages.name: Lakshadweep Samudram
tourPackages.open: Domestic and foreign tourists (foreigners with tourist visa); booked online only.

tourPackages.name: Coral Reef / Swaying Palm / Marine Wealth Awareness
tourPackages.open: Referenced on the site; itineraries vary year to year.

dos: Confirm your tour reservation before leaving home.
Bring your own medicines and toiletries — only ordinary varieties are available on the islands.
Use the SPORTS representative on board / on the island if you have difficulties.
donts: Do not litter the land or the water.
Do not pick up corals as souvenirs — it is a punishable offence.
Do not use alcohol or intoxicants — there is prohibition on ALL islands except Bangaram.
Do not carry narcotics or drugs — a punishable offence.
Do not swim or sunbathe nude — it is prohibited.
Do not go outside your island's lagoon without SPORTS permission and a proper escort.
Do not pluck coconuts — the trees are privately owned and unauthorised plucking is theft.
Do not book a return journey for your arrival day — ship timings are unpredictable.

Agatti.role: The gateway island — the only one with an airstrip; 'virtual gateway to the islands'.
Agatti.features: One of the most beautiful lagoons in Lakshadweep; the runway runs almost the length of the thin island.
Agatti.accommodation: A 20-bed tourist complex is described on the SPORTS site; the site also carries a standing notice that there is currently NO government-permitted resort at Agatti and that claims to the contrary are false.
Agatti.access: Flights from Kochi (~1h30). Onward boat/helicopter to Bangaram and Thinnakara; boats to Kavaratti/Kadmat in the fair season.
Agatti.activities: Lagoon water sports, snorkelling, glass-bottom boat, diving.

Bangaram.role: The only uninhabited resort island in Lakshadweep; 'tiny teardrop-shaped island'.
Bangaram.features: Shares a lagoon with Thinnakara and Parali; at night phosphorescent plankton on the coral sand can glow bluish.
Bangaram.access: Flight to Agatti, then boat or (season permitting) helicopter transfer.
Bangaram.notes: The one island where alcohol is permitted. Pitched at 'discerning exclusive' tourists.
Bangaram.activities: Snorkelling, diving, kayaking, deep-sea fishing, lagoon.

Thinnakara.role: A small island in Bangaram's lagoon, run as a tented beach camp by SPORTS.
Thinnakara.activities: Snorkelling, kayaking, lagoon swimming, glass-bottom boat, day trips to Bangaram/Parali.

Kavaratti.role: The capital / administrative headquarters and most developed island.
Kavaratti.features: 52 mosques across the island — the finest is the Ujra (Jama-Ath) mosque, said to have a well with curative water. Calm lagoon good for water sports, swimming and snorkelling.
Kavaratti.attractions: Marine aquarium; Dolphin Dive Centre (scuba); glass-bottom boats.
Kavaratti.access: Flight to Agatti then boat (Taratashi package), or by ship (Samudram). Boats from Agatti in the fair season.
Kavaratti.packages: Taratashi (Kavaratti resort); part of the Samudram cruise.

Kadmat.role: A long, very thin island (~8 km long, ~550 m at its widest) known for diving.
Kadmat.features: Broad shallow lagoon on the west (water sports); narrow eastern lagoon; long sandy beaches and sand banks at the southern tip. Tourist huts among palm groves facing the lagoon. Water Sports Institute on the island.
Kadmat.diving: Laccadives (Lacadives, Mumbai) Kadmat Dive School — one of India's finest dive centres, 20-50 m visibility, courses ~1 Oct to 1 May.
Kadmat.access: Boat from Agatti in the fair season; ship packages. 'Non-Indians are also permitted to visit this island.'
Kadmat.packages: Marine Wealth Awareness Programme (2-4 days on the island).

Kalpeni.role: An atoll with the main island Kalpeni plus islets Tilakkam and Pitti, and the uninhabited Cheriyam nearby.
Kalpeni.features: A huge storm bank of coral debris along the eastern/south-eastern shore, thrown up by a violent storm in 1847. Koomel Beach with two bathing huts and change rooms. Historically notable as the place where girls first went to school in the islands.
Kalpeni.activities: Swimming, snorkelling, reef-walking, kayaks and sailboats.
Kalpeni.nearby: Pitti islet is a protected seabird breeding site (Pitti Bird Sanctuary) — not a landing spot for tourists.

Minicoy.role: The isolated southernmost island, ~200 km south of the main group, culturally distinct and close to the Maldives.
Minicoy.features: Crescent-shaped, ~10.6 km long (second largest island after Andrott). One of the largest lagoons, with the small uninhabited islet Viringili on its south. A cluster of 11 villages, each with an elected head (Bodukaka). Mahl language. Famous for the 'Lava' dance and the colourful communal race boats (jahadhoni).
Minicoy.attractions: A ~300-ft (light said built 1885, British-era) lighthouse; an important tuna fishing centre with a tuna canning/processing factory.
Minicoy.accommodation: 3 tourist cottages and a 20-bed tourist home; bathing huts with change rooms; water sports.
Minicoy.access: Ship only (Samudram cruise and Swaying Palm package) — no airstrip or helipad.
